references: Creative Tech 1 · Project 0. This tutorial takes you from an empty Blender file to a web page where a visitor clicks a part of your object, the part animates away, a fact appears, and a language model responds to it. You will model a simple block object, render it to sprite sheets, wire it into HTML, CSS and JavaScript, and then call a model three ways: Ollama on your own computer, Claude, and OpenAI. Work through it in order. Each part ends with a checkpoint you can test.
conclusion_future_work:
To begin with, this film festival has provided invaluable feedback for my final project. I have gained a wealth of ideas—ranging from VR and AR technologies to various 3D modeling techniques—that empower me to boldly express my vision through engaging interactivity. Drawing inspiration from successful case studies, I aim to create spatial and 3D installations that surprise and delight audiences. I was particularly impressed by the "Water World" and "Slwata" projects, and I plan to incorporate elements of their installation designs into my own work. Experiencing the latest games has further deepened my interest in the intersection of interactivity and art, and I hope to create equally outstanding work in the future.

results_discussion:
To begin with, at 1:10, I experienced "Water Body"—a truly spectacular spatial installation. I lay back on a very comfortable sofa, and as the show began, the sound of rain washed over me, instilling a deep sense of calm and tranquility. I watched as countless raindrops gradually merged into streaks, then into flowing currents, eventually transforming into an entire aquatic world—an Earth made of water. It was absolutely magnificent; I felt as though I had become one with the installation. Closing my eyes, I savored the relaxing, soothing sensation evoked by the water. When it finally ended and the visuals faded away, the experience left a lasting impression that lingered in my mind.
Next, at 2:05, I experienced *SAWATA*—truly the most delightful surprise among all the VR installations I tried. After putting on the headset and selecting "English" via a hand-grabbing gesture, the film began. I observed the visuals and 3D modeling, followed by a guide: a small fish leaping repeatedly through the water to lead me toward a specific location. Upon reaching that spot, I was fully immersed in a three-dimensional VR world; everything felt incredibly realistic. Looking around—to the side or to the left—I felt as though I was truly present within that environment. The film introduced the lives of the island's inhabitants. As the story unfolded, the simulated water level rose steadily—from my ankles to my waist, and finally submerging my head—allowing me to experience what it was like for the islanders to survive a torrential downpour. Yet, their resilience and strength of spirit, revealed as the narrative progressed, served to uplift and encourage me. Along the way, I could interact with small 3D objects by grabbing them, which would then provide further guidance—a truly engaging feature. By the end of the film, the waters receded, and everything resolved beautifully. It was a truly spectacular experience.
title: A Trip to London and Making a Spirit Board—The Beginning of the Website
introduction: It has been a truly enjoyable week. We visited the 70th London Film Festival together—an incredibly fascinating event where the interactive installations really blew me away. My father gained a wealth of knowledge and experienced a unique technological culture, which provided valuable insights and inspiration for my final project. At the same time, I began to unlock the secrets of coding and have started building my own website; I look forward to seeing the results next week.
